h1_old: How to Dismiss a Traffic Ticket in Wichita Falls with Defensive Driving

faqs.q: How much does it cost to dismiss a ticket in Wichita Falls?
faqs.a: The court cost is typically up to about $144 ($169 in a school zone), set by each court — some area courts charge less. The TDLR-approved course is separate; ours is $28. Check your court's page for the exact amount.

faqs.q: Can I take the Wichita Falls defensive driving course online?
faqs.a: Yes. Once the court approves your request, a TDLR-approved 6-hour course can be completed fully online. Every Wichita Falls-area court accepts a state-approved online course.

faqs.q: My ticket is from Burkburnett / Iowa Park / Holliday, not Wichita Falls. Does that change things?
faqs.a: The legal steps are the same, but you deal with that city's court — and Holliday and Archer City are in Archer County, with their own fee, request method, and deadlines. Open its page in the table above.

faqs.q: How long do I have to finish?
faqs.a: Generally 90 days after the court approves the request. Request the course by your appearance date first, and don't pay the ticket — paying is a guilty plea and a conviction.

faqs.q: Does a dismissal keep it off my insurance?
faqs.a: Yes. A driving safety course dismissal keeps the charge off your driving record under Texas law, so it can't raise your insurance — unlike paying, which is a conviction.

courts.name: Wichita Falls Municipal Court
courts.note: You'll need a certified Type 3A driving record from Texas DPS to submit with your certificate. Court fee: $144.
